name: Birth of Titans from Gaia and Ouranos
description: Gaia and Ouranos give birth to the Titans, giant beings who will rule the cosmos. Among them are Kronos and Rhea.

name: Kronos Castrates Ouranos
description: Kronos attacks his father Ouranos with a sickle, castrates him, and takes control of the cosmos. This marks the end of Ouranos's rule.

name: Birth of Zeus
description: Rhea secretly bears Zeus in Crete while Kronos swallows a stone, believing it to be his newborn son. Zeus is hidden and raised by nymphs in secret.

name: Titanomachy Begins
description: Zeus reaches manhood and challenges his father Kronos. The war between Titans and Olympians erupts, shaking the cosmos with divine fury.

name: Titanomachy Concludes
description: After a decade-long war, Zeus and the Olympians defeat the Titans. Kronos and the defeated Titans are imprisoned in Tartarus.

name: Prometheus Steals Fire from Olympus
description: The Titan Prometheus defies Zeus by stealing divine fire from Olympus and giving it to humanity, enabling civilization and technology.

name: Prometheus Chained to the Caucasus
description: Zeus orders Prometheus chained to a rock in the Caucasus Mountains. An eagle eats his immortal liver daily; the liver regenerates each night, ensuring eternal suffering.

name: Creation of Pandora
description: Zeus orders the creation of Pandora, the first woman, as punishment for Prometheus's theft. Hephaestus crafts her, and she is given a sealed box.

name: Pandora Opens the Box
description: Curiosity overwhelms Pandora and she opens the forbidden box. Evils and miseries escape into the world, bringing suffering to humanity forever.

name: Hades Abducts Persephone
description: While gathering flowers, the maiden Persephone is seized by Hades and taken to the underworld to be his bride. Demeter begins her desperate search.

name: Demeter's Grief Freezes the World
description: Grief-stricken Demeter causes eternal winter. Crops fail, and humanity faces starvation. The earth becomes barren as the goddess mourns her lost daughter.

name: Divine Compromise: Persephone's Seasonal Return
description: Zeus negotiates a compromise. Persephone spends half the year with Hades in the underworld and half with Demeter above. This cycle creates seasons.

name: Danaë Imprisoned in Bronze Tower
description: King Acrisius imprisons his daughter Danaë in a bronze tower to prevent her from bearing a son who might kill him. However, Zeus reaches her as golden rain.

name: Birth of Perseus
description: Danaë gives birth to Perseus, son of Zeus. She and her infant are cast into the sea in a wooden chest but survive and wash ashore on an island.

name: Perseus Receives Divine Gifts
description: The gods grant Perseus divine artifacts: Hermes gives winged sandals and an adamantine sickle; Athena provides a magical shield that reflects any gaze.

name: Perseus Slays Medusa
description: Using Athena's shield as a mirror, Perseus sees Medusa's reflection without meeting her deadly gaze. He strikes with the adamantine sickle and severs her head.

name: Zeus Deceives Alcmene
description: Zeus, disguised as her husband Amphitryon, lies with Alcmene. She later bears both Heracles (son of Zeus) and Iphicles (true son of Amphitryon).

name: Birth of Heracles
description: Heracles is born as the greatest hero of Greek mythology. Even as an infant, he strangles serpents sent by jealous Hera, displaying his extraordinary strength.

name: Hera's Curse: Heracles's Madness
description: Hera's jealousy drives Heracles to madness. In his frenzy, he kills his own wife and children, bringing deep shame and sorrow.

name: The Twelve Labors Begin
description: To atone for his madness-induced crimes, Heracles accepts twelve impossible labors imposed by King Eurystheus. His first labor: slay the Nemean Lion.

name: Heracles Slays the Nemean Lion
description: Heracles's arrows prove useless against the Nemean Lion's impenetrable hide. He discovers the lion is vulnerable internally and strangles it, then uses its claws as a weapon.

name: Heracles Defeats the Lernaean Hydra
description: Heracles battles the nine-headed Hydra. Each head he cuts off regenerates into two new heads. He eventually succeeds by cauterizing each neck stump to prevent regrowth.

name: Heracles Captures Cerberus
description: The final labor: Heracles descends to the underworld to capture Cerberus, the three-headed guard dog. He overcomes the beast and brings it to the surface.

name: Theseus Volunteers as Tribute to the Minotaur
description: Prince Theseus volunteers to be part of Athens's tribute to Crete, hoping to slay the Minotaur and free his people from this horrible annual tax.

name: Ariadne's Thread: The Escape Plan
description: Princess Ariadne of Crete falls in love with Theseus and gives him a ball of thread to navigate the Labyrinth. He ties one end at the entrance to mark his way.

name: Theseus Slays the Minotaur
description: Theseus enters the Labyrinth and confronts the Minotaur. Using his strength and cunning, he defeats the creature and follows Ariadne's thread back to the entrance.

name: Jason Gathers the Argonauts
description: Jason assembles the greatest heroes of Greece for the quest to find the Golden Fleece. The crew includes Heracles, Theseus, and many other legendary heroes.

name: The Argo Sets Sail
description: The legendary ship Argo, built by craftsmen with divine assistance, sets sail from Greece toward distant Colchis in search of the Golden Fleece.

name: The Argonauts Pass the Clashing Rocks
description: The Argo faces the Symplegades, two floating islands that crash together. Through skill and speed, Jason navigates through the narrow passage, a crucial test of the ship and crew.

name: Jason Obtains the Golden Fleece
description: With Medea's magical help, Jason retrieves the Golden Fleece from Colchis. They escape as King Aeetes pursues them, ultimately returning to Greece with the prize.

name: Paris Abducts Helen
description: Prince Paris of Troy, guided by Aphrodite's promise, sails to Sparta and abducts the beautiful Helen, wife of King Menelaus. This act sparks the greatest conflict of the age.

name: Greek Alliance Assembles
description: Menelaus and his brother Agamemnon rally the Greek city-states. All the greatest heroes—Achilles, Ajax, Odysseus—gather to sail to Troy and recover Helen.

name: Greek Fleet Sails to Troy
description: A thousand ships carrying the might of Greece set sail for Troy. The greatest military expedition ever assembled begins its voyage across the Aegean Sea.

name: Ten Years of Siege and Battle
description: For a decade, Greeks and Trojans clash before Troy's impenetrable walls. Heroes fall, alliances shift, and divine powers intervene. Achilles and Hector emerge as champions.

name: Achilles Slays Hector
description: Achilles and Hector meet in single combat before Troy's gates. Achilles, enraged by the death of Patroclus, kills the great Trojan prince, changing the fate of the war.

name: Construction of the Trojan Horse
description: After years of stalemate, Odysseus devises a brilliant strategy. Greeks build a massive wooden horse, hiding elite warriors inside. The horse is left as a supposed gift.

name: Trojans Accept the Wooden Horse
description: The Trojans, believing the siege is over, drag the massive horse inside their walls as a victory trophy or offering to the gods. This proves to be their fatal mistake.

name: Fall of Troy
description: Under cover of night, Greek warriors emerge from the horse. They open the city gates, allowing the Greek army to pour in. Troy burns and falls after ten years of conflict.

name: Odysseus Begins Journey Home
description: After Troy's fall, Odysseus sets sail for Ithaca. However, Poseidon's anger at the blinding of his son Polyphemus dooms him to ten years of wandering.

name: Odysseus Encounters the Cyclops
description: Odysseus and his men are trapped in a cave by Polyphemus, a giant Cyclops. Odysseus blinds the monster, but this enrages Poseidon who becomes his relentless enemy.

name: Odysseus Resists the Sirens
description: The Sirens' deadly song lures sailors to their deaths, but Odysseus has his men bind him to the mast while they plug their ears with wax. He alone hears their song.

name: Odysseus Returns to Ithaca
description: After ten years of trials, Odysseus finally reaches Ithaca. He finds his faithful wife Penelope waiting and his son Telemachus grown to manhood.
